data.context_preview:
For an additional order of the existing strawberry concentrate item, document the item identity, requested quantity, reason, required date, demand basis, and any unresolved information. The Purchasing Team should review master data, inventory, reservations, demand, inbound plans, supplier conditions, and the status of existing purchase requests; supplier selection or confirmation is outside this review. Manufacturing Planning should assess production-plan and material-readiness impact. Budget, unit price, and approval status must not be inferred; if financially relevant, they remain confirmation items for the appropriate finance function. Accumulate the review evidence and unresolved items, then refer any official purchase-request submission, budget allocation, approval, supplier confirmation, purchase order, external communication, or system write to an authorized person. The review is read-only and does not constitute purchasing execution or approval.

input.grounding:
For a quarterly F&B profitability review, use the procedure for exchange-rate and raw-material price changes together with the business-plan assumption review. Required evidence includes the target lemon carbonated beverage and quarter, exchange-rate and raw-material price inputs, their dates and coverage, existing cost assumptions and sources, BOM and manufacturing-cost evidence, demand and revenue assumptions, and any production-plan or operating constraints that could affect the result. Finance should distinguish calculable scenarios from missing inputs and calculate cost impacts; Business Planning should assess demand, revenue, profitability, and plan-assumption impacts. Record scenario-specific effects, uncertainty, limitations, additional-input requests, and final confirmed inputs. Manufacturing Planning is consulted only when production plans, BOM, materials, capacity, or operating constraints could change the assessment. The review does not approve budgets, prices, investments, accounting entries, payments, or official plan changes. Any such decision must be separately escalated with the accumulated analysis and evidence to an authorized person.

data.context_preview:
The retrieved procedures applicable to introducing allulose as a new production ingredient require documenting the ingredient, intended products and lines, target timing, BOM/planning linkage, material master data, supply readiness, operating constraints, and unresolved items. Procurement should review material master data, supply conditions, and registration readiness; R&D, Quality, and Production review only where new specifications, formulation, quality, or production impacts are actually identified. Process-condition or yield impacts should be documented separately with process and production records and routed to Process, Equipment, Quality, or R&D as applicable. Quality review should capture the applicable specification, test records, deviations or unresolved requirements, and any need for additional testing. Supplier and lot traceability, allergen and labeling review, line clearance, sanitation, operator training, in-process checks, and formulation-validation details are not specified in the retrieved context. These reviews do not themselves constitute ingredient approval, product approval, quality release, production authorization, product disposition, labeling approval, or system change; formal registration, release, production-input, and other final decisions must be made by an authorized person under separate procedures.

input.grounding:
The retrieved procedures applicable to introducing allulose as a new production ingredient require documenting the ingredient, intended products and lines, target timing, BOM/planning linkage, material master data, supply readiness, operating constraints, and unresolved items. Procurement should review material master data, supply conditions, and registration readiness; R&D, Quality, and Production review only where new specifications, formulation, quality, or production impacts are actually identified. Process-condition or yield impacts should be documented separately with process and production records and routed to Process, Equipment, Quality, or R&D as applicable. Quality review should capture the applicable specification, test records, deviations or unresolved requirements, and any need for additional testing. Supplier and lot traceability, allergen and labeling review, line clearance, sanitation, operator training, in-process checks, and formulation-validation details are not specified in the retrieved context. These reviews do not themselves constitute ingredient approval, product approval, quality release, production authorization, product disposition, labeling approval, or system change; formal registration, release, production-input, and other final decisions must be made by an authorized person under separate procedures.

Finance reviews budget, cost allocation, cost, transfer, and management-accounting evidence and limitations; business planning separately reviews business, profitability, planning, and operational impacts. An authorized person makes the formal approval or change decision. IT reviews ERP/MDM data impact only after an approved or formally decided business change with confirmed system impact, including identifiers, field mapping, validation, audit traceability, and rollback conditions. Budget allocation/approval, accounting posting, and ERP implementation are separate procedures and are not completed by the review. The retrieved evidence requires the applicable period to be documented but does not define effective-date rules, F&B-specific controls, or additional evidence requirements specifically for next-quarter changes.
